walkthrough.heading: OFFICE WORKFLOW — STEP BY STEP
This is the handoff guide for the person entering bills, cards, checks, deposits, and job-cost allocations.
Amounts in U.S. dollars unless otherwise noted.
1. ONE-TIME SETUP
Use Setup to maintain Jobs, Vendors, and Equipment. Equipment setup stores permanent facts only; never change its job or line item each time it moves.
2. WHEN AN INVOICE ARRIVES
Enter the vendor and invoice in Transactions. A PO is helpful for matching and approval, but it is not required just to record the invoice.
3. PO DECISION
Choose Matched to PO when one exists. Choose No PO Required for approved items that do not require a PO. Choose Missing - Get Approval when the purchase should have had a PO or approval is uncertain.
4. SPLIT THE INVOICE
Use one allocation row for each job/line item. Enter Invoice Total only on the first row. Repeat Vendor and Invoice # on every split row. Difference must equal zero.
5. EQUIPMENT USAGE
Equipment: enter one row per machine per stay on a job - start date, end date, job, machine. The cost is charged to that job. Line items are not used for equipment.
6. HAND TO ACCOUNTANT
The Transactions sheet is the accounting source. Equipment Allocation is a separate job-cost/reclassification schedule and must not be added a second time.
EXAMPLE — SEACOAST INVOICE FOR FERN HILL: WATER + SEWER MATERIALS

Assume Seacoast invoice SC-1001 totals $10,000.00: $6,000.00 is water-main material and $4,000.00 is sanitary-sewer material. There is no PO. Enter two allocation rows as shown. If the purchase was authorized and no PO is required, select No PO Required. If company policy expected a PO, select Missing - Get Approval.
Vendor

Why these accounts: the line item 8" DIP Water Main maps Materials to 5230, while 8" PVC Sewer Main maps Materials to 5240. Both rows use Job = Fern Hill. The total allocations equal the $10,000.00 invoice, so Difference is zero.

Important accounting control: If the office records a rental invoice in Transactions and also records that machine in Equipment Allocation, the Equipment Allocation is a management/job-cost allocation schedule—not a second expense. The accountant can use it to reclassify costs among line-item equipment accounts. Do not add it again to cash, AP, or total company expense.
7. REVIEW THE REPORTS

Use Job Costing to choose a job and see costs by line item. Use Account Summary to see totals by the full Chart of Accounts. Finish the Month-End Checklist before handing the workbook and source documents to the accountant.
